title: Getting Started with ethsign
text: Ethereum uses original (pre-FIPS-202) Keccak, SHA3-256. keccak256() accepts UTF-8 string raw bytes returns plain raw(32):
code: keccak256("") # the canonical empty-string Ethereum vector #>  [1] c5 d2 46 01 86 f7 23 3c 92 7e 7d b2 dc c7 03 c0 e5 00 b6 53 ca 82 27 3b 7b #> [26] fa d8 04 5d 85 a4 70 keccak256(as.raw(c(0x12, 0x34))) #>  [1] 56 57 0d e2 87 d7 3c d1 cb 60 92 bb 8f de e6 17 39 74 95 5f de f3 45 ae 57 #> [26] 9e e9 f4 75 ea 74 32

title: Getting Started with ethsign
text: EIP-712 dominant signing scheme EVM venues. ethsign builds 0x1901-prefixed signing digest single struct atomic field types (string, uint64, uint256, bool, address, bytes32). domain named list; types ordered list list(name, type); message supplies field values name. Hyperliquid usdSend user action, exact reproduction official Hyperliquid Python SDK testnet vector: need digest (example verify , sign later $sign_digest()), compute directly eip712_digest():
code: domain <- list(   name = "HyperliquidSignTransaction",   version = "1",   chainId = 421614,   verifyingContract = "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" )  types <- list(   list(name = "hyperliquidChain", type = "string"),   list(name = "destination", type = "string"),   list(name = "amount", type = "string"),   list(name = "time", type = "uint64") )  message <- list(   hyperliquidChain = "Testnet",   destination = "0x5e9ee1089755c3435139848e47e6635505d5a13a",   amount = "1",   time = 1687816341423 )  sig <- signer$sign_typed_data(domain, "HyperliquidTransaction:UsdSend", types, message) sig #> <eth_signature> #>   r: 0x637b37dd731507cdd24f46532ca8ba6eec616952c56218baeff04144e4a77073  #>   s: 0x11a6a24900e6e314136d2592e2f8d502cd89b7c15b198e1bee043c9589f9fad7  #>   v: 27 digest <- eip712_digest(domain, "HyperliquidTransaction:UsdSend", types, message) digest #>  [1] ca cf 75 85 cc 49 ca 60 c6 c5 fb 30 01 e2 26 c0 ca 03 c4 62 52 c8 93 ee a5 #> [26] 74 c7 89 07 b7 ce be

title: Getting Started with ethsign
text: ecrecover() Ethereum’s signature--address recovery: given signed digest (r, s, v) triple, returns address produced signature. Recovering test key’s address closes loop:
code: rsv <- as_rsv(sig) recovered <- ecrecover(digest, rsv$r, rsv$s, rsv$v)  recovered #> [1] "0x14791697260e4c9a71f18484c9f997b308e59325" recovered == signer$address #> [1] TRUE

title: Getting Started with ethsign
text: $sign_message() applies EIP-191 personal_sign prefix ("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n" + nbytes + text) hashing signing. digest behind Sign-Ethereum (SIWE) “sign message log ” flows: relying party verifies login way – reconstruct prefixed digest ecrecover claimed address:
code: login <- "example.com wants you to sign in with your Ethereum account" msig <- signer$sign_message(login)  as_hex(msig) #> [1] "0x6b083a7d1440b7d3dd0f56bc30f725422f02e8365b7b9f4211b6cf04cb4635147e4becaa09d02c9c77bed3b139c4f06cf7fbf81dc645b61c8dde154870ba03991b" body <- charToRaw(enc2utf8(login)) prefix <- c(   as.raw(0x19),   charToRaw("Ethereum Signed Message:\n"),   charToRaw(as.character(length(body))) ) login_digest <- keccak256(c(prefix, body))  mrsv <- as_rsv(msig) ecrecover(login_digest, mrsv$r, mrsv$s, mrsv$v) == signer$address #> [1] TRUE

title: Ethereum Signing Primitives
text: ethsign creates cryptographic signature crypto wallet makes – digital “stamp” proves request came wallet authorizes – directly R. Pure-R Ethereum EVM wallet signing primitives: keccak-256 hashing, secp256k1 ECDSA Ethereum recovery id low-s normalisation, EIP-712 typed-data signing, EIP-191 personal_sign, address derivation. cryptographic primitives needed authenticate sign orders EVM venues Hyperliquid Polymarket, native dependencies beyond gmp openssl. note responsibility. package handles private keys produces signatures can authorize real transactions. responsible use keeping keys safe.

title: Ethereum Signing Primitives
text: ethsign signing maths plus small signer object holds key memory. whole scope. wallet application. : hold move funds, read balances, connect chain RPC node, broadcast, submit, track transactions. : derive Ethereum address private key, hash data keccak-256, build EIP-712 typed-data digest, produce canonical (r, s, v) ECDSA signature, deterministically, recover signing address signature (ecrecover). resulting signature – post venue, embed raw transaction, present login – tooling.

title: ethsign 0.0.1
text: Signer (EthSigner, via eth_signer() / eth_signer_random()): holds secp256k1 private key memory exposes $address plus three signing paths – $sign_digest() (arbitrary 32-byte digest), $sign_typed_data() (EIP-712), $sign_message() (EIP-191 personal_sign, SIWE / login digest). key normalised raw(32), never exposed, never printed. Hashing & EIP-712: keccak256() (original pre-FIPS-202 Keccak) eip712_digest(), builds 0x1901-prefixed typed-data signing digest single struct atomic field types (string, uint64, uint256, bool, address, bytes32). Keys & addresses: eth_keygen() fresh random private key eth_address() address derivation key. Signatures: canonical eth_signature object two serializations – as_rsv() ({r, s, v} object form, e.g. Hyperliquid) as_hex() (65-byte concatenated form, e.g. Polymarket). Verification: ecrecover() recovers signing address digest (r, s, v), inverse check EthSigner’s output.

title: ethsign 0.0.1
text: Pure R. native build; dependencies gmp (big-integer curve arithmetic) openssl (keccak, HMAC-SHA256, secure randomness). Deterministic. ECDSA nonces generated RFC 6979 (HMAC-SHA256 DRBG), given key digest always yield signature – signing fully offline reproducible, network funds. Ethereum-correct. EIP-2 low-s normalisation v = 27 + recid recovery byte; load-time self-test aborts system openssl ships FIPS-202 SHA3 Keccak name. Verified. Reproduces EIP-712 spec example (“Ether Mail” domain separator) official Hyperliquid Python SDK signing vectors (usdSend, withdraw3) exactly. Validated. Public inputs return shapes checked assert package; package dogfoods assert roxyassert (generated argument/return contracts exported assert_type_eth_signature).
